title: A ransomware tabletop exercise

injects.title: 06:00 Help desk
injects.text: Staff at three branches cannot open shared files. A note on the file server says the files are encrypted and names a group.

injects.title: 08:00 Leak site
injects.text: The group's leak site lists the company and claims 40 GB of member records, with a sample of names and account numbers.

injects.title: 11:00 A reporter calls
injects.text: A local reporter asks Communications to confirm a breach of member data by 13:00 for an afternoon story.

injects.title: Day 2, 09:00 Backups
injects.text: IT reports that the last two weeks of backups were reachable from the domain and are partly encrypted. Older copies are offline and clean.

injects.title: Day 2, 14:00 The CFO
injects.text: The CFO: 'Insurance will cover it. Let's just pay and get the files back.'

objective: Train, test and evaluate incident management with tabletop, walk-through and simulation exercises
secondaryObjectives: Manage incident response communications: reporting, notification and escalation
Develop an incident response plan aligned with the business continuity and disaster recovery plans

sources.cite: ISACA, CISM Exam Content Outline (exam from 2026-11-03): Domain 1 Information Security Governance; Domain 2 Information Security Risk Management; Domain 3 Information Security Program
sources.note: Read as HTML on 2026-11-14 for REQ-272 and not re-read. Domain 1 part B covers the information security strategy and the business case, budget and resources; Domain 2 part B covers risk treatment against the risk appetite; Domain 3 part B covers program metrics reported to senior leadership. The course's objective wording is its own.

Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the CTEP page: the packages include 'template exercise objectives, scenarios, and discussion questions', templates for 'exercise planners, facilitators / evaluators, and participants', 'a feedback form ... and an After Action Report'; scenarios include ransomware. The injects, organization and times in this exercise are the author's.

sources.cite: FEMA, Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP), revised February 2020
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the HSEEP page: 'Exercise evaluation assesses the ability to meet exercise objectives and capabilities'; results are documented in an After-Action Report/Improvement Plan covering 'strengths, areas for improvement, capability performance, and corrective actions'. The page does not itself say corrective actions get owners and dates; that practice is the author's reading of an improvement plan and is marked as such.

sources.cite: NIST SP 800-84, Guide to Test, Training, and Exercise Programs for IT Plans and Capabilities (September 2006)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the NIST publication page, which gave only the title, number and dates (created 2006, page updated May 20, 2023); the guide's text on tabletop exercises was not read. Named as the federal guide for IT plan exercises; to verify.

sources.cite: SEC, Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure (final rule, July 2023): Form 8-K Item 1.05
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of Hunton Andrews Kurth's summary of the final rule (not the SEC's own text): a material incident is disclosed within four business days after the company determines it is material, and that determination is made 'without unreasonable delay after discovery'. Cited only for why counsel's materiality assessment starts early; the exercise's company is not assumed to be listed and no deadline is scored.

brief.situation: You lead Harbor Mutual's incident response team, a fictional insurer, through a two-hour tabletop exercise, and you play the incident manager. The facilitator reads a ransomware scenario in injects from Monday 06:00. Make the decisions the plan asks of you in time, bring the right people in, keep what goes outside the company cleared, and find where the plan fails, so the after-action report can fix it.
handover: The response plan names the roles: incident manager, IT operations, legal counsel and privacy, communications, and the COO as executive sponsor.
This is an exercise: nothing leaves the room. A decision made here is judged as if it were real.
howItWorks: The clock is the scenario's time. Each discussion takes scenario minutes; the facilitator's next inject arrives on the same clock and stops the wait.
The table shows each inject (one still waiting for the team's decision is marked), the roles, the communications and the decision log.
When the exercise ends you write the after-action report and explain your reasoning.

source.note: First inject at the scenario's start, 06:00.
The backup inject on day 2 at 09:00.
The CFO's question on day 2 at 14:00.
The facilitator ends the scenario on day 2 at 18:00.

hotwash.question: For the after-action report: how the team decided at each inject, what went outside the company and how, and what the exercise showed about the plan.

parts.label: Decisions in time
parts.criteria: Activates the plan at the first inject; brings counsel and privacy in at the leak claim and preserves evidence; restores from clean copies in business-impact order; takes each decision within about an hour of the inject.
parts.modelAnswer: We declared at 06:00, had counsel in by 08:20, and chose to restore from the clean offline copies in the business impact analysis's order.

parts.label: Communications and authority
parts.criteria: Briefs the executive sponsor; the reporter gets a holding statement reviewed by counsel before it goes out; payment is an executive decision with counsel, law enforcement, the insurer and a sanctions check, not the CFO's or the team's alone.
parts.modelAnswer: The COO was briefed early; the reporter got a counsel-reviewed holding statement before 13:00; the payment question went to the executive with counsel, after law enforcement, the insurer and a sanctions check.

parts.label: What the plan lacks
parts.criteria: Names the gaps the exercise exposed (no insurer contact, no out-of-band channel, a stale restore order) and gives each an owner and a date in the improvement plan.
parts.modelAnswer: Three gaps: no insurer contact, no out-of-band channel, a restore order that ignores the BIA. Each has an owner and a date in the improvement plan.

source.note: Each inject's decision within an hour of scenario time.
Every gap found has an owner and a date in the improvement plan.

outside.label: A decision outside the plan
outside.narrative: In the scenario, the team said something to the press counsel had not seen, denied what it could not deny, or paid without the checks the decision needs. In a real incident that would have done the harm.

noReport.narrative: The exercise found problems, and none of them will be fixed: there is no improvement plan.

expertPath.text: Declare and activate the plan; brief the COO; ask how the team and staff talk if email is down; notify staff by text and phone tree.
Bring counsel and privacy in at the leak claim and preserve evidence; ask who calls the insurer.
Give the reporter a holding statement counsel has reviewed.
Ask for the restore order, then restore from clean copies in business-impact order; send the payment question to the executive with counsel, law enforcement, the insurer and a sanctions check.
In the after-action report, give each gap an owner and a date.

exercised.headline: Good: the exercise did its job
exercised.body: A tabletop succeeds by finding what the plan lacks while it is cheap to fix. You decided in time, kept what went out cleared, and left each gap with an owner.

partly.headline: Partly tested
partly.body: The criteria show what was missed: a late decision, a role left out, or a gap found but not owned.

outside.headline: A decision the plan would not allow
outside.body: Statements go out after counsel reviews them, and paying is an executive decision with counsel, law enforcement, the insurer and a sanctions check. Saying so in an exercise is how a team learns it.

noReport.headline: Nothing will change
noReport.body: Without an improvement plan, the gaps the exercise found will still be there when the real incident comes.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No after-action report was written before the run's limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Activate the plan at the first inject and brief the executive sponsor. At the leak claim, bring counsel and privacy in and preserve evidence: counsel starts the notification and materiality assessment. Give the reporter a holding statement counsel has reviewed. Restore from the clean offline copies in business-impact order. Paying is an executive decision with counsel, law enforcement, the insurer and a sanctions check. Use the exercise to find what the plan lacks: an insurer contact, an out-of-band channel and a current restore order. Give each an owner and a date.
